Reading Service Tiers Like a Pro

5 min read · Updated November 2026 · Free · Written for Kenya
Share: WhatsApp X Facebook Telegram LinkedIn

The cheapest service per 1,000 is often the most expensive per follower that stays. The listing tells you which one you're buying, if you know where to look.

Every service name is a short spec sheet: platform, action, quality tier, refill cover and speed. Most buyers read only the price. This lesson shows you how to read the rest, so you buy the right thing for the job.

Anatomy of a service name

Part of the nameExampleWhat it really tells you
Platform + actionInstagram Followers / TikTok ViewsWhat you get, and what link to paste (profile or post)
Quality tierReal Mix / High QualityHow credible the accounts look to a human visitor: photos, posts, activity
Refill coverNo Refill / 30-Day RefillWhether drops inside that window get topped back up
SpeedInstant Start / gradual over 24-48hHow fast it lands, and how much it looks like a spike
Min / MaxMin 20, Max 10,000The smallest test you can run and the most one order can take

Why numbers drop, and why refills exist

Platforms clean house all the time. In May 2026 Instagram removed bots and long-inactive accounts in one big sweep, and even the biggest accounts lost millions of followers overnight. Any service, paid or not, can be hit by a sweep like that.

A refill service covers that risk for a set window. If the count drops inside the window, it gets topped back up. If you see a drop on a refill order, open a ticket with the order ID. No Refill is cheaper because you carry that risk yourself.

✗ MYTH

"Refill" means the numbers are permanent.

✓ REALITY

Refill covers drops inside the stated window (say 30 days). After that, normal platform clean-ups can still remove accounts. Match the refill length to how long you need the number to hold, like a launch month or a campaign.

Match the tier to the job

What the order is forTier to preferSpeed to prefer
Testing a service for the first timeAny, small quantityWhatever's listed. You're testing the flow
A business page customers will judgeHigh Quality / Real MixGradual over 1-3 days
A time-sensitive post (launch, event)Mid or high tierInstant Start, modest quantity
A big number on a page with little historyHigh tier with refillSplit across several days
💡 What most buyers miss

Do the math per lasting follower, not per 1,000. Here's an illustration, not a price quote: a KES 100 service that keeps 70% after a month costs about KES 0.14 per remaining follower. A KES 130 service with a refill that holds close to 100% costs about KES 0.13. The cheaper listing was the dearer one.

📋 Before-you-pay checklist (save in your notes)
1. Action matches link? (followers = profile link, likes/views = post link)
2. Tier matches the job? (customers or brands will look = higher tier)
3. Refill window covers how long I need it? (Y/N)
4. Speed: gradual unless the post is time-sensitive
5. Quantity looks believable next to my current numbers?
6. Account/post public and username final?
⚡ Quick check

Two follower services: A costs less and has No Refill; B costs a bit more with a 30-day refill. You need the page to look established for a month-long launch. Which is usually the better buy?

Platform clean-ups happen (Instagram ran a huge one in May 2026). For a launch you need numbers that hold for the whole month, so the refill window is part of the price.

🧠 Key takeaways
  1. A service name packs platform, action, tier, refill and speed into one line. Read all five.
  2. Drops come from platform clean-ups. Refill covers them only inside its window.
  3. Compare cost per follower that lasts, not cost per 1,000.
  4. Higher tiers and gradual speed suit pages that customers or brands will judge.
